summary: Native-stone 1941 fire lookout on Custer Peak in the Black Hills, successor to a 1911 wooden tower, with a long roster of named staff through 1964.

facts.design: Two-story native stone cab, 14x14 ft with catwalk, architect W. Ellis Groben

access.note: Located in Black Hills National Forest, publicly accessible; not an overnight rental.

events.note: First fire lookout on Custer Peak built of wood, with shutters but no glass, on a railing-less platform.
Wooden tower replaced with a cupola building (NHLR gives 1935; firelookout.com suggests the 1920s).
Current two-story native stone tower built, 14x14 ft cab with catwalk, designed by W. Ellis Groben.
Frank Tower's recorded tenure as lookout runs 1917 to 1944.
James Curry and E.A. Nelson recorded as lookouts.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, October 13, 1990.
Forest Service employees carried out a stabilization project on the tower near Deadwood.

evidence.supports: 1911 wood lookout with shutters, no glass, no railings; replaced by cupola by 1935; current two-story stone structure built 1941, 14x14 ft cab with catwalk; architect W. Ellis Groben
evidence.quote: The first fire lookout atop Custer Peak on the Nemo Ranger District of the Black Hills National Forest was built of wood in 1911. It had shutters but no glass, and it sat atop a platform without railings. By 1935 it had been replaced with a cupola building. The current structure is two stories high and was built of native stone in 1941.

evidence.supports: Established 1911, cupola cabin replacement in the 1920s, present 2-story stone cab built 1941; named lookout staff list
evidence.quote: Established with frame cabin the 1911, replaced by a cupola cabin in the 1920s?, the present 2-story stone and frame cab, constructed in 1941, is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register. Known lookout personnel: 1921: Hans Miller; 1917-1944: Frank Tower; 1946: James Curry & E.A. Nelson; 1947-1948: Jim Meyers; 1949-1963: John Sloss; 1964: Evelyn Sorheim.

evidence.supports: Fire towers built nationwide after 1910 fires; 2008 stabilization project near Deadwood; vandalism risk noted
evidence.quote: Fire towers were constructed across the nation after devastating fires in 1910.
near Deadwood during a stabilization project in 2008.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the cupola replacement to by 1935; firelookout.com tentatively suggests the 1920s (with a question mark). Both are noted in the story.

sources.publisher: National Historic Lookout Register / U.S. Forest Service
